rationale: Rationale: Sunken eyes and a sunken fontanelle indicate SEVERE dehydration; per IMNCI Plan C the child must receive urgent IV rehydration (Ringer's lactate/normal saline) and be admitted. Anti-diarrhoeals are contraindicated in children, and ORS alone is inadequate for severe dehydration. (Ref: Kenya IMNCI; MOH Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols.)

question_text: Q6. The activities the nurse engages in during the preparatory phase of a home visit include:
options: b) Clarifying the source of the referral
answer: Answer: B) Clarifying the source of the referral
rationale: Rationale: The preparatory (pre-visit) phase is done before leaving for the home: the nurse reviews the records and CLARIFIES the source and reason for the referral, gathers relevant information and plans the visit. Locating the house occurs during the visit, and recording/reporting occurs after it. (Ref: Community Health Nursing - the home visit process.)

question_text: Q7. During pregnancy the uterine muscle fibres increase:
options: a) 10 times in length, 5 times in thickness
b) 20 times in length, 10 times in thickness
c) 5 times in length, 10 times in thickness
d) 15 times in length, 10 times in thickness
answer: Answer: A) 10 times in length, 5 times in thickness
rationale: Rationale: Uterine enlargement in pregnancy is mainly by hypertrophy of existing muscle fibres, which increase greatly in length (about ten-fold) and to a lesser degree in thickness/width. Of the options the closest to this is 10 times in length. (Ref: Myles Textbook for Midwives - the uterus in pregnancy.)

question_text: Q8. The ischial spines are designated as an important landmark in labour and delivery because the distance between the spines is a measurement of the:
options: b) Outlet of the birth canal
answer: Answer: D) Narrowest pelvic diameter
rationale: Rationale: The interspinous diameter (between the ischial spines, ~10.5 cm) is the NARROWEST diameter of the pelvic cavity/mid-pelvis; the ischial spines are also the reference point ('station 0') for assessing descent of the presenting part. (Ref: Myles Textbook for Midwives - the female pelvis.)

question_text: Q9. A newborn suffering from hyper-bilirubinaemia can be treated with:
answer: Answer: D) Intravenous 5% dextrose
rationale: Rationale: Besides phototherapy (and exchange transfusion when severe), adequate hydration with intravenous fluids such as 5% dextrose promotes bilirubin excretion and corrects dehydration. Salicylates and sulpha drugs are AVOIDED because they displace bilirubin from albumin and increase the risk of kernicterus. (Ref: MOH Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols - neonatal jaundice.)

question_text: Q10. Respiratory distress syndrome (of the newborn) is characterised by:
options: a) Underdeveloped alveoli and deficient surfactant production
b) Decreased pulmonary resistance and underdeveloped alveoli
c) Uninflatable alveoli and overproduction of surfactant
d) Poor alveolar ventilation and pulmonary vasodilatation
answer: Answer: A) Underdeveloped alveoli and deficient surfactant production
rationale: Rationale: Neonatal RDS (hyaline membrane disease) results from immaturity of the lungs - underdeveloped alveoli with DEFICIENT surfactant - leading to alveolar collapse, atelectasis and impaired gas exchange. (Ref: MOH Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols; Nelson Paediatrics.)

question_text: Q11. Preventive measures for ophthalmia neonatorum include:
options: a) Administering systemic penicillin within one hour after birth, isolation of the baby
b) Instillation of penicillin eye drops after birth, taking an eye swab for culture and sensitivity
c) Treatment of abnormal vaginal discharge prenatally, application of 1% tetracycline eye ointment within one hour of birth
d) Treatment of all vaginal discharges prenatally, application of 3% tetracycline eye ointment within one hour of birth
answer: Answer: C) Treatment of abnormal vaginal discharge prenatally, application of 1% tetracycline eye ointment within one hour of birth
rationale: Rationale: Ophthalmia neonatorum is prevented by treating maternal genital infection (abnormal vaginal discharge) during the antenatal period and by routine eye prophylaxis - application of 1% tetracycline eye ointment (or equivalent) to both eyes within one hour of birth. (Ref: MOH Kenya newborn care; WHO STI guidelines.)

question_text: Q12. Causes of blood coagulation disorders during pregnancy include:
options: b) Dehydration, intrauterine foetal death, pre-eclampsia
c) Ante-partum haemorrhage, eclampsia, intrauterine sepsis
d) Amniotic fluid embolism, malnutrition, iso-immunization
answer: Answer: C) Ante-partum haemorrhage, eclampsia, intrauterine sepsis
rationale: Rationale: Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) in pregnancy is triggered by conditions that release thromboplastins or cause endothelial damage - antepartum haemorrhage (especially abruptio placentae), severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, intrauterine sepsis, intrauterine fetal death and amniotic fluid embolism. Option C lists three established triggers. (Ref: Myles Textbook for Midwives; MOH Kenya.)

question_text: Q13. Omphalitis predisposes a newborn baby to:
options: b) Asphyxia neonatorum, constipation, umbilical hernia
c) Apnoeic attacks, haemorrhagic disease of the newborn, neonatal tetanus
answer: Answer: D) Jaundice, septicaemia, hepatitis
rationale: Rationale: Omphalitis (infection of the umbilical stump) gives organisms direct access to the bloodstream and, via the umbilical vein, to the liver - predisposing the baby to septicaemia, jaundice and hepatic infection (hepatitis/liver abscess). (Neonatal tetanus is also linked to cord contamination, but the triad that follows blood/portal spread of omphalitis is jaundice, septicaemia and hepatitis.) (Ref: MOH Kenya Basic Paediatric Protocols; Myles.)

question_text: Q14. The 1st stage of labour is defined as the period from the onset of:
options: a) Labour pains (true labour) to full dilatation of the cervix
b) Labour pains to crowning of the head
c) True labour to delivery of the baby
d) True labour to dilatation of the cervix
answer: Answer: A) Labour pains (true labour) to full dilatation of the cervix
rationale: Rationale: The first stage of labour extends from the onset of true (regular, effective) labour contractions to FULL dilatation of the cervix (10 cm). It comprises a latent and an active phase. The period to delivery of the baby is the second stage. (Ref: Myles Textbook for Midwives.)

question_text: Q15. The indications for the first vaginal examination during labour are to:
options: a) Confirm labour, determine descent, identify the presenting part
b) Determine engagement, confirm lie of the second twin, and examine cervical tears
c) Confirm crowning, ascertain whether membranes have ruptured, assess
d) Confirm cervical dilatation, determine state of the perineum, assess progress of labour
answer: Answer: A) Confirm labour, determine descent, identify the presenting part
rationale: Rationale: The first vaginal examination in labour is performed to confirm the diagnosis of labour and assess progress - it identifies the presenting part and position, determines descent/station, and assesses cervical effacement and dilatation and the state of the membranes. (Ref: Myles Textbook for Midwives.)

question_text: Q16. The signs that indicate placental separation include:
options: a) Lengthening of the cord, a gush of blood, rising and hardening of the uterus
b) Rising and hardening of the uterus, heavy bleeding, lengthening of the cord
c) Shortening of the cord, rising and hardening of the uterus, a gush of blood
d) Heavy bleeding, an urge to bear down, lengthening of the cord
answer: Answer: A) Lengthening of the cord, a gush of blood, rising and hardening of the uterus
rationale: Rationale: Signs of placental separation in the third stage are: lengthening of the umbilical cord, a small gush of blood, and the uterus rising in the abdomen and becoming firm, hard and globular (rounded). Heavy bleeding and cord SHORTENING are not normal signs of separation. (Ref: Myles Textbook for Midwives - third stage of labour.)

question_text: Q17. Nordette is an example of:
answer: Answer: B) A monophasic low-dose pill
rationale: Rationale: Nordette is a combined oral contraceptive in which every active pill contains the same fixed dose of oestrogen and progestogen (levonorgestrel + ethinyloestradiol) - i.e. a monophasic low-dose pill. (Ref: MOH Kenya National Family Planning Guidelines.)

question_text: Q18. A contact disease caused by bacteria is:
answer: Answer: B) Impetigo
rationale: Rationale: Impetigo is a contagious skin infection caused by bacteria (Staphylococcus aureus and/or Streptococcus pyogenes) and spread by contact. Scabies and pediculosis are parasitic (mite/lice) infestations. (Trachoma is bacterial but is an eye disease; the classic 'contact skin disease caused by bacteria' answer is impetigo.) (Ref: Communicable disease / Community Health Nursing.)

question_text: Q19. A child growing within the normal developmental milestones will be able to walk at the age of:
answer: Answer: C) 12-18 months
rationale: Rationale: Independent walking is normally achieved between about 12 and 18 months of age (most children walk by 12-15 months). Sitting is achieved around 6 months and standing with support before walking. (Ref: Kenya IMNCI / MOH Kenya Child Health - developmental milestones.)

question_text: Q20. The approximate calorie needs for young children under five years are:
answer: Answer: D) 100 calories/kg/day
rationale: Rationale: Young children require roughly 100 kilocalories per kilogram of body weight per day - far higher per kg than adults because of rapid growth and high metabolic rate. (Ref: MOH Kenya/WHO nutrition guidelines; Nelson Paediatrics.)

question_text: Q21. The scientific name for ringworm of the scalp is:
answer: Answer: C) Tinea capitis
rationale: Rationale: Dermatophyte (ringworm) infections are named by site: tinea capitis = scalp, tinea corporis = body, tinea pedis = feet (athlete's foot), tinea versicolor (pityriasis versicolor) = trunk discoloration. (Ref: Communicable disease / dermatology.)

question_text: Q22. Diseases of agricultural hazards include:
answer: Answer: B) Zoonotic diseases, toxic hazards
rationale: Rationale: Agricultural occupational hazards classically include zoonotic diseases (transmitted from animals, e.g. brucellosis, anthrax) and toxic chemical hazards (pesticides, fertilisers, organophosphates). (Ref: Occupational/Environmental Health - Community Health Nursing.)

question_text: Q23. The international health agencies that were instrumental in starting the Bamako Initiative are:
answer: Answer: D) WHO, UNICEF
rationale: Rationale: The Bamako Initiative (1987) was launched jointly by WHO and UNICEF to revitalise primary health care and improve drug availability through community financing/cost-sharing. (Ref: Community Health Nursing - history of PHC.)

question_text: Q24. The safe noise exposure level that does not cause damage to the tympanic membrane is:
answer: Answer: C) 85 dB
rationale: Rationale: The recommended safe occupational noise exposure limit is about 85 decibels (over an 8-hour day); prolonged exposure above this risks noise-induced hearing damage. (Ref: Occupational Health - Community Health Nursing.)

question_text: Q25. The major practice roles of the occupational health nurse include:
answer: Answer: A) Clinician, administrator
rationale: Rationale: The core practice roles of the occupational health nurse are as clinician (direct care/first aid/health surveillance) and administrator/manager of the occupational health service, in addition to educator, consultant and researcher roles. (Ref: Occupational Health Nursing.)

question_text: Q26. The drugs that may reduce the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives include:
answer: Answer: B) Phenytoin, Griseofulvin
rationale: Rationale: Hepatic enzyme-inducing drugs accelerate metabolism of contraceptive steroids and reduce their effectiveness - these include phenytoin and griseofulvin (and rifampicin, carbamazepine, barbiturates). The option in which BOTH drugs are enzyme inducers is phenytoin + griseofulvin. (Ibuprofen, digoxin and chlorpheniramine do not reduce contraceptive efficacy.) (Ref: Pharmacology; MOH Kenya FP Guidelines.)

question_text: Q27. The vector that carries the causative organism for trypanosomiasis is:
answer: Answer: D) Tsetse flies
rationale: Rationale: African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness, caused by Trypanosoma brucei) is transmitted by the bite of the tsetse fly (Glossina). Sand flies transmit leishmaniasis, black flies onchocerciasis, and fleas plague. (Ref: Communicable disease - Community Health Nursing.)

question_text: Q28. The measures that would appropriately improve the health of the elderly include:
options: a) Mental health services, STI services
c) Home safety programmes, home-based services
answer: Answer: C) Home safety programmes, home-based services
rationale: Rationale: Health promotion for the elderly focuses on safety and supporting independence - home safety programmes (preventing falls/injury) and home-based care services are the most appropriate measures for this age group. (Ref: Gerontological / Community Health Nursing.)

question_text: Q29. Prevalence rate is defined as the number of:
options: a) Old and new cases of a specified disease existing at a given time
b) New cases of a disease in a population over a period of time
c) Old cases of a specified disease existing at a given time
d) Deaths from a specified disease or condition at a given time
answer: Answer: A) Old and new cases of a specified disease existing at a given time
rationale: Rationale: Prevalence is the total number of existing cases (both old and new) of a disease present in a defined population at a given point (or period) in time. New cases over time describe incidence; deaths describe mortality. (Ref: Epidemiology - Community Health Nursing.)

question_text: Q30. Some of the developmental tasks of a beginning family are:
options: a) Family planning, stabilizing the family unit
b) Family planning, relating to kin network
c) Relating to kin network, maintaining a stable marriage
d) Stabilizing the family unit, socializing children
answer: Answer: B) Family planning, relating to kin network
rationale: Rationale: In Duvall's family life-cycle, Stage I (the beginning/married-couple family) tasks include establishing a mutually satisfying marriage, RELATING to the kin network, and FAMILY PLANNING (deciding about children). Socialising children belongs to later stages. (Ref: Family Health / Community Health Nursing - Duvall's developmental tasks.)

question_text: Q31. Some of the indirect client services provided by the community health nurse include:
options: a) Supervising the care provided, teaching
b) Teaching, health planning with consumers
d) Record keeping, supervising the care provided
answer: Answer: D) Record keeping, supervising the care provided
rationale: Rationale: Indirect care services are those performed on behalf of clients but not in direct face-to-face care - such as record keeping/documentation and supervising the care provided by others. Teaching, planning with consumers and bedside care are DIRECT services. (Ref: Community Health Nursing - roles of the CHN.)

question_text: Q32. The components of the biological environment include:
answer: Answer: B) Water supplies, food
rationale: Rationale: The biological environment comprises living things and the products of living things that surround and sustain humans - including food sources and water supplies (which also harbour micro-organisms, plants and animals). Toxic substances, geographical features and natural resources are elements of the PHYSICAL environment. (Ref: Community Health Nursing - the environment and health.)

question_text: Q33. The major service system of the community that is usually the focus of the citizen and the leadership of the community is:
answer: Answer: C) Economic system
rationale: Rationale: The economic system (production, employment, income and resources) is the service system that most preoccupies community members and their leaders, because livelihoods and the community's capacity to support all other systems (including health) depend on it. (Ref: Community Health Nursing - community as a system/sub-systems.)

question_text: Q34. The demographic parameters the community health nurse will examine while conducting a community diagnosis include:
answer: Answer: A) Distribution, morbidity
rationale: Rationale: Demographic parameters describe the population - its size, distribution/composition and vital statistics such as morbidity and mortality. Genetics and transport services are not demographic parameters. (Ref: Community Health Nursing - community diagnosis.)

question_text: Q35. Vector-borne diseases include:
answer: Answer: D) Plague, leishmaniasis
rationale: Rationale: Vector-borne diseases are transmitted by arthropod vectors - plague by fleas and leishmaniasis by sand-flies. Dysentery is faeco-oral (water/food-borne) and rubella is spread by respiratory droplets, so neither is vector-borne. (Ref: Communicable disease / Epidemiology - Community Health Nursing.)

question_text: Q36. A type of schizophrenia characterised mainly by delusions of persecution and auditory hallucinations is:
answer: Answer: B) Paranoid
rationale: Rationale: Paranoid schizophrenia is dominated by delusions (especially of persecution and/or grandeur) and auditory hallucinations, with relative preservation of cognition and affect. Disorganized type shows disorganized speech/behaviour and flat affect; catatonic shows marked psychomotor disturbance. (Ref: Psychiatric/Mental Health Nursing.)

question_text: Q37. Postpartum depression (early postnatal mood disturbance) typically appears on:
answer: Answer: A) The 3rd and 4th day
rationale: Rationale: The early, transient postnatal mood disturbance ('postpartum/maternity blues') typically appears about the 3rd-4th day after delivery, coinciding with hormonal changes and the onset of lactation, and usually resolves spontaneously within a few days. (True postpartum depression has a later, more insidious onset over weeks.) (Ref: Myles Textbook for Midwives; Mental Health Nursing.)

question_text: Q38. A type of epilepsy in which psychological features are common is:
answer: Answer: D) Temporal lobe epilepsy
rationale: Rationale: Temporal lobe epilepsy (complex partial seizures) is characteristically associated with psychological/psychic phenomena - auras, deja vu, fear, hallucinations of smell/taste, automatisms and mood/behavioural changes. (Ref: Psychiatric/Mental Health Nursing; Neurology.)

question_text: Q39. Reciprocal inhibition involves:
options: a) Continuous presentation of the phobic stimulus
b) Hierarchical introduction of anxiety-producing stimuli
c) Elimination of behaviour by introduction of a more adaptive behaviour which is incompatible with the unacceptable behaviour
d) Punishment during which the patient is removed from the environment where the unacceptable behaviour is being exhibited
answer: Answer: C) Elimination of behaviour by introduction of a more adaptive behaviour which is incompatible with the unacceptable behaviour
rationale: Rationale: Reciprocal inhibition is a behaviour-therapy principle in which an undesirable response (e.g. anxiety) is inhibited by simultaneously eliciting an incompatible response (e.g. relaxation) - the adaptive behaviour replaces and is incompatible with the maladaptive one. (Ref: Psychiatric/Mental Health Nursing - behaviour therapy.)

question_text: Q40. A behaviour-therapy technique used in the treatment of sexual aversion disorder is:
answer: Answer: A) Sensate focus
rationale: Rationale: Sensate focus (graded, non-demand pleasuring exercises) is the behavioural technique used for sexual aversion and related sexual dysfunctions to reduce performance anxiety. The squeeze technique is used for premature ejaculation. (Ref: Psychiatric/Mental Health Nursing - sexual disorders.)

question_text: Q41. Co-dependence means:
options: a) Dysfunctional behaviour evident among members of the family of a chemically dependent person
b) Dysfunctional behaviour evident among members of a social group that abuse the same chemical substances
c) Two or more people portray dependence on the same substance
d) Dysfunctional behaviour evident among members of the social group of a chemically dependent person
answer: Answer: A) Dysfunctional behaviour evident among members of the family of a chemically dependent person
rationale: Rationale: Co-dependence describes the dysfunctional behaviours and relationships adopted by FAMILY members of a chemically dependent person - they over-adapt to, enable and revolve their lives around the addicted individual. (Ref: Psychiatric/Mental Health Nursing - substance use disorders.)

question_text: Q1. The male pelvis compared with the female pelvis is ___ and ___:
answer: Answer: A) Narrower and deeper
rationale: Rationale: The male (android) pelvis is narrower and deeper, with a heart-shaped brim and a narrow sub-pubic arch, making it unsuitable for childbirth. The female (gynaecoid) pelvis is wider and shallower with a rounded brim. (Ref: Myles Textbook for Midwives - the female pelvis.)

question_text: Q2. Which of the following statements is TRUE about contraceptive implants?
answer: Answer: D) Norplant - 6 capsules
rationale: Rationale: Norplant is the original 6-capsule levonorgestrel implant (effective ~5 years). Jadelle has 2 rods (5 years), Implanon 1 rod (3 years) and Sino-implant (Zarin) 2 rods - so the only correct statement is that Norplant consists of 6 capsules. (Ref: MOH Kenya National Family Planning Guidelines.)

question_text: Q3. In the management/prevention of ophthalmia neonatorum:
options: a) Treat the mother for syphilis and apply 1% tetracycline eye ointment (TEO) at birth
b) Treat the eye with penicillin drops at birth
c) Treat abnormal vaginal discharge prenatally and apply 3% TEO within one hour of birth
d) Treat abnormal vaginal discharge prenatally and apply 1% TEO within one hour of birth
answer: Answer: D) Treat abnormal vaginal discharge prenatally and apply 1% TEO within one hour of birth
rationale: Rationale: Ophthalmia neonatorum is prevented by treating maternal genital infection (abnormal vaginal discharge) antenatally and giving routine eye prophylaxis with 1% tetracycline eye ointment to both eyes within one hour of birth. (Ref: MOH Kenya newborn care; WHO STI guidelines.)
